title: Hourly to Annual Pay Calculator: Tax, Super, and Salary Sacrificing Calculator Insights
description: Convert your hourly rate to annual pay with our calculator. Includes tax, Medicare, super, and explains how a salary sacrificing calculator can refine your take-home estimate.

faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to annual pay?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply by 52. Our calculator assumes a standard 38-hour week for full-time work. For part-time or casual hours, adjust the weekly hours accordingly. The result is your gross annual income before tax and other deductions.

faqs.q: Does the calculator account for salary sacrificing?
faqs.a: No. Our calculator estimates pay without salary sacrifice arrangements. If you have a salary packaging agreement, your taxable income is reduced, which affects tax and Medicare. Use a dedicated salary sacrificing calculator to see how packaging a car or super contributions changes your net pay. The Australian Taxation Office provides guidance on effective arrangements.

faqs.q: What tax and super assumptions does the calculator use?
faqs.a: It uses the 2026–27 resident tax rates: tax-free threshold up to $18,200, then 15% to $45,000, 30% to $135,000, 37% to $190,000, and 45% above that. Medicare levy is 2% (using 2025–26 single reduction thresholds). Super guarantee is 12% of ordinary earnings, paid on top, up to the $270,830 maximum contribution base. These are estimates only.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Your Hourly to Annual Conversion

Knowing your annual pay from an hourly rate is essential for budgeting, comparing job offers, or planning your tax. The basic formula is simple: multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply by 52 weeks. For a full-time employee working 38 hours per week, that’s **hourly rate × 38 × 52**. This gives your gross annual income before any deductions.

For example, the National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour. At 38 hours, that’s $1004.90 per week, or $52,254.80 per year. If you’re paid fortnightly, simply double the weekly amount: $2009.80.

### Award Rates and Casual Loading

Many employees are covered by an award that sets higher minimum rates. The Fair Work Ombudsman publishes [pay guides](/blog) for each award, including penalty rates and allowances. Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base rate – for the minimum wage, that’s $33.05 per hour. Our calculator includes a checkbox to add casual loading; **do not enter a rate that already includes the loading**.

## Tax, Medicare, and Your Take-Home Pay

Once you have your annual gross figure, tax and the Medicare levy reduce your net income. For the 2026–27 income year, resident tax rates are:

- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income. Our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) calculator applies these rates to estimate your after-tax annual and fortnightly amounts.

### How Salary Sacrificing Changes the Picture

If you have a salary sacrifice arrangement, your taxable income is lower because you agree to receive less salary in exchange for benefits like a car or extra super contributions. This can reduce the tax you pay. The Australian Taxation Office explains that an effective salary sacrifice arrangement must be entered before you perform the work and you cannot access the sacrificed amount.

Our calculator does not include salary sacrificing. To see how packaging affects your net pay, use a dedicated **salary sacrificing calculator**. It will account for fringe benefits tax (FBT), employee contributions, and the impact on your taxable income. For instance, the ATO’s example shows that salary sacrificing a car can increase net disposable income when employee contributions are made.

## Superannuation Paid on Top

Your employer must pay super guarantee of 12% on your ordinary earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per quarter. This is paid **on top** of your salary, not deducted from it. For an annual gross of $52,254.80, super would be about $6,270.58 per year. Our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page explains how salary sacrificed super contributions are treated as employer contributions and are not subject to FBT.

### Fortnightly Pay and Budgeting

If you’re paid fortnightly, your gross pay is weekly pay × 2. For the minimum wage, that’s $2009.80 per fortnight. After tax and Medicare, your net fortnightly amount will be lower. Use our calculator to see the exact figures for your rate.

## Important Disclaimer

Annual pay here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.
